identification: Four-piece 1970s hifi: (1) Pioneer SA-7300 stereo integrated amplifier (silver face, model read off the front panel), dusty, a vendor tag '5584/3 3pce' stuck on the front; (2) Technics direct-drive turntable (Technics logo on the label plate, model number not legible) in a grey/champagne plinth with S-shaped tonearm, front-right control panel with lever controls, felt mat, dust cover present, headshell/cartridge fitted (cartridge unidentified); styling fits the late-1970s Technics SL-1600/SL-1610/SL-1700/SL-1300 family; (3)-(4) pair of walnut-wrapped bookshelf/floor speakers with black square-cube foam 'Quadrex' grilles, the JBL L100 Century look; no badge visible, so genuine JBL L100 vs lookalike is unconfirmed. Not tested.

viewing_check: Turn the speakers round: a genuine JBL L100 has a JBL label/serial plate on the back and 12-inch white-cone woofer (123A) behind the foam; any other badge means lookalike. Read the Technics model on the plate in front of the tonearm and check the platter spins and arm/cartridge are intact. Power up the Pioneer and check both channels, scratchy pots and the speaker selector.
